  "review_kind": "critique",
  "reviewer_label": "fresh-no-context-performance-reviewer",
  "overall_assessment": "Changes required for the automated candidate: the public conversation list retains an unbounded nested-message hydration path despite bounding its parent page. This is a separate exposure from the corrected negative-limit and latest-IN findings.\n\nThe negative-limit correction is sound for scalar inputs: defaults remain 200/100, finite positive values are floored and capped at 500, and list lookahead remains bounded at 501. The call-through HTTP/PostgreSQL regressions provide meaningful fail-first evidence. PERF-01's latest-IN remediation also remains resolved: the supplied plans show direction-constrained index access, 500 probes, zero direction-filtered OUT rows and preserved expired/no-IN/tie semantics. Selected non-window references avoid the window query. The 30-conversation endpoint measurement establishes batched binding, credential and window reads, but does not establish a bound on the initial nested message retrieval.\n\nAdherence is otherwise acceptable within the reviewed scope: the narrow Channel port, operation factories, common outbound owner, sole MessageAcceptance owner and provider boundaries preserve D01–10 without adding future providers or capabilities. Elegance and structural soundness are acceptable; correcting the remaining read path needs a bounded query change rather than architectural expansion.\n\nOperational evidence is appropriately qualified. The reported all28261 result covers 588 tests with current product/context hashes and served-bundle matching. Index storage and write observations are descriptive: approximately 6.86 MB and 15.9 ms versus 6.47 ms for the sampled 1,000-row writes. Transactional migration limits and accelerated rollback probes are distinguished honestly. The guard now detects the specified swallowed-command mutations and exercises failure propagation through cleanup. Remote CI remains not_run. Preserved-database activation and operator IN/OUT remain correctly gated after prerequisite audits and must still block Local-Implemented closure. This review used only the embedded package and performed no execution.",
  "recommended_path": "Resolve PERF-R3-01 within the approved read/test paths, collect request-bound evidence for actual nested-message work, and rerun the canonical all after source changes. Record PERF-R3-02 as non-blocking debt. Preserve prior resolved dispositions and complete prerequisite audits before OrderedStep6; retain Pending delivery until operational proof and final gates are satisfied.",
  "performance_position": "mixed",
  "elegance_position": "acceptable",
  "structural_soundness_position": "acceptable",
  "operational_fit_position": "mixed",
  "findings": [
    {
      "finding_id": "PERF-R3-01",
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "performance",
      "formalizable_hint": "yes",
      "candidate_rule_level": "project",
      "title": "Public conversation pages still fetch unbounded message histories",
      "rationale": "PublicConversationsController.conversations loads multiple parent conversations with include.messages ordered by createdAt/id and take: 1. With the supplied Prisma 6 configuration, which does not enable relationJoins, multi-parent nested pagination uses the query loading strategy and applies the per-parent limit in memory; the child query can retrieve every matching message for those conversations. A page containing a long-history conversation therefore has unbounded database transfer and application hydration despite the 500-parent cap. The supplied EPS counters measure binding, credential and latest-IN queries, while the 500-reference EXPLAIN measures the separate window projection; neither measures this initial child fetch. This is a concrete resource-exhaustion path in the touched public listing and conflicts with D07/SCOPE-06's bounded-read premise. The approved managed latest-IN index does not resolve this separate hydration behavior.",
      "suggested_action": "Retrieve latest-message fields through a database-bounded batched top-one-per-conversation query, preserving ordering, response fields and lookahead semantics. Avoid per-conversation application queries. Capture the actual endpoint SQL and execution work with multiple parents and a deep message history, proving that child retrieval stays bounded by the page rather than total history; then run fresh canonical validation.",
      "affected_paths": [
        "api-app/src/surfaces/public/conversations.controller.ts",
        "api-app/test/number-onboarding-pcv.e2e-spec.ts",
        "api-app/prisma/schema.prisma"
      ]
    },
    {
      "finding_id": "PERF-R3-02",
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "operational_fit",
      "formalizable_hint": "yes",
      "candidate_rule_level": "project",
      "title": "Repeated limit parameters now produce an uncaught type error",
      "rationale": "limitePublico calls valor.trim() before checking its runtime type. Express represents repeated query parameters such as limit=17&limit=18 as an array, regardless of the Record<string, string> annotation. Both touched GET endpoints consequently return HTTP 500 for that input. The previous Number-based expression fell back to the default for this repeated-value case. This remains bounded and is non-blocking compatibility debt, not a severe performance exposure.",
      "suggested_action": "Accept unknown input at the normalization boundary and handle non-string values explicitly, preferably using the existing default behavior. Add request-level coverage for repeated values on both endpoints.",
      "affected_paths": [
        "api-app/src/surfaces/public/conversations.controller.ts",
        "api-app/test/api-publica.e2e-spec.ts"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
